Thanks for the time on Friday. As we prepare a Dedicated sizing recommendation for BrightGrid's pilot, a few targeted inputs will let us produce a compact estimate and a safe fallback routing plan. I've attached a lightweight sizing_template.xlsx — the asks below are intentionally narrow and focused on what affects GPU occupancy and p99 latency the most. - Percent of requests that are chat-style (multi-turn with KV cache reuse) vs single-turn generation.

- Session shape: avg turns per session and percent of sessions that hit >8 turns.
- P95/P99 latency SLO target and acceptable fallback latency (e.g., 500ms / 2s).
- Allowed fallbacks: degrade to smaller model (quantized) / route to dedicated burst pool / queue with async callback — which are acceptable?
- Any KV cache reuse expected across requests from the same session or user id? If yes, rough cache hit rates.

Attachments: sizing_template.xlsx (simple sheet for sample telemetry).

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa on the sizing engine side once we have your sample histogram so they can scope GPU SKU mix and kernel choices.

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the checklist. Attached is a quick export (prod_token_histogram.csv) from our telemetry window for the last 30 days plus inline answers below. Forgive the roughness — pulled directly from our logs.

Inline answers:
- Typical business-hours QPS: 18 QPS sustained (09:00–18:00 PST). Peak burst windows: short spikes up to ~420 QPS (1–3 minute bursts) around new feature rollouts / newsletter sends.
- Chat-style vs single-turn: ~62% chat-style (we keep KV per session for personalization), 38% single prompt responses.
- Prompt length distribution: median 18 tokens, 75th 54, 95th 320. Response length distribution: median 120 tokens, 75th 290, 95th 1,200. Attached histogram shows a heavy tail around scheduled report generation.
- Session shape: avg 5 turns/session; ~9% of sessions exceed 8 turns (power users).
- Latency SLO: P95 token-to-token target 150ms; P99 we aim for <850ms. If load requires fallback, acceptable latency up to 3s for non-interactive batch tasks; interactive flows should not exceed 1.2s ideally.
- Allowed fallbacks: we prefer (in order) 1) route to quantized model variant (slightly lower quality acceptable), 2) queue with async callback for non-interactive jobs, 3) no cross-region routing (data residency).
- KV cache reuse: yes — estimated session KV hit 70% for chat flows; report generation usually has low reuse.

Attachments: prod_token_histogram.csv (attached).

Let me know if you want a sampled anonymized payload for profiling.

Cheers,

Thanks for the thread, Kim. Quick technical read and recommended deliverables for BrightGrid: please find concise bullets below that we can paste into the customer note. Also added a short attachment (kernel_recommendation_notes.md) into our shared drive with microbenchmarks.

Observations from telemetry:
- Heavy-tailed response lengths (95th ~1.2k) mean worst-case token generation time dominates tail latency; these will inflate GPU occupancy during bursts.
- KV reuse (~70%) is good — enabling prefix/KV cache with session affinity can cut effective per-request token generation by ~40% for chat flows. That materially reduces sustained occupancy.

Recommendations (customer-facing bullets):
- Recommended GPU mix: H100-style instances for the burst pool (best p99s on long sequences) + one or two A100-class nodes for steady-state background processing. Approx starting footprint: 6 H100 GPUs dedicated to handle 420 QPS burst headroom with 1.5x safety margin assuming average response token lengths ~300 during bursts. (We can tighten after a 7-day pilot telemetry run.)
- Caching & batching: enable prefix/KV caching and session affinity for chat flows; configure a dynamic batching window of 10–25ms for the burst pool to maximize throughput without adding >20ms to p99.
- Fallback routing policy (implement in order): 1) When occupancy >72% on burst pool, route eligible requests to quantized model variant pinned to dedicated quant pool. 2) For non-interactive heavy jobs (like report generation), move to an async queue with guaranteed callback and soft timeout of 3s. 3) Only if both above exhausted, throttle with 429 and offer degraded response.
- Per-tenant caps: cap single-tenant burst allocations to 200 QPS by default, can raise to 350 QPS with commit; remaining headroom needs organizational approval.
- Kernel & quantization notes: H100 kernels give better per-token latency for long sequences; see kernel_recommendation_notes.md in our drive for exact kernel selection and quant profiles we recommend (llm-q8_0 / dynamic).

Deliverables to send Samir by EOD tomorrow:
- Short summary (bullets above)
- Initial sizing estimate (numbers above) with assumptions clearly listed
- Suggested client-side routing policy (one-page)
- Pilot telemetry checklist (what we'll collect during the 7-day run)

Attachments: kernel_recommendation_notes.md (added to Drive), and I'll export a short occupancy table (kv_cache_profile.pdf) for the customer-facing packet.

-Karthik
